G5344.name: Felix
G5344.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G5344.brief: Roman governor of Judea; heard Paul's case.
G5344.short: Felix was a Roman governor of Judea who heard the case against Paul and kept him in custody for two years.

G5347.name: Festus
G5347.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G5347.brief: Roman governor of Judea; heard Paul's case; sent him to Rome.
G5347.short: Porcius Festus succeeded Felix as the Roman governor of Judea and heard Paul's case, ultimately sending him to Rome for trial.

G5323.name: Phanuel
G5323.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G5323.short: Phanuel, the father of Anna, a prophetess who witnessed the infant Jesus at the temple.

G5371.name: Philemon
G5371.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G5371.brief: Recipient of Paul's letter, Colossian slave owner
G5371.short: Philemon, a Christian from Colossae to whom Paul wrote a letter appealing for the reconciliation with his runaway slave, Onesimus.

G5372.name: Philetus
G5372.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G5372.short: Philetus, along with Hymenaeus, was a false teacher who had strayed from the truth and taught that the resurrection had already taken place.

G5376J.name: Philip
G5376J.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G5376J.brief: One of the seven deacons, evangelized in Samaria
G5376J.short: Philip, one of the seven deacons chosen by the early church in Jerusalem, who preached the gospel in Samaria and baptized an Ethiopian eunuch.

G5376I.name: Philip
G5376I.desc: Tetrarch living at the time of the New Testament
G5376I.short: Philip, the son of Herod the Great, who ruled as tetrarch of Iturea and Traconitis during the time of John the Baptist's ministry.

G5376G.name: Philip
G5376G.desc: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
G5376G.brief: One of the twelve apostles of Jesus
G5376G.short: Philip, one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus, from Bethsaida in Galilee.

G5376H.name: Philip
G5376H.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G5376H.brief: Herod Antipas' brother, first husband of Herodias
G5376H.short: Philip, the half-brother of Philip the Tetrarch, and Herod Antipas who took Philip's wife, leading to John the Baptist's condemnation of their marriage.

G5378.name: Philologus
G5378.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G5378.brief: Believer in Rome greeted by Paul
G5378.short: Philologus, a Christian in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings in his letter to the Romans.

G5393.name: Phlegon
G5393.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G5393.brief: Believer in Rome greeted by Paul
G5393.short: Phlegon, a Christian in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings in his letter to the Romans.

G5359.name: Philadelphia
G5359.brief: One of the seven churches in Asia Minor
G5359.short: Philadelphia was one of the seven churches in Asia Minor addressed in the Book of Revelation, known for its faithfulness and endurance.

G5375.name: Philippi
G5375.brief: A city in Macedonia visited by Paul
G5375.short: Philippi was a city in Macedonia where Paul founded a church and experienced persecution, imprisonment, and a miraculous deliverance.

G5330.name: Pharisee
G5330.brief: A strict Jewish sect known for legalism and hypocrisy
G5330.short: The Pharisees were a Jewish sect known for their strict observance of the law and oral traditions, often clashing with Jesus over matters of ritual purity, Sabbath regulations, and His claims to divine authority (<ref="Matthew 23; Luke 11:37-54">Matthew 23; Luke 11:37-54</ref>).
